findings.description: The requirement leaves the configuration bytes covered by the CRC and the treatment of the stored reference undecided. CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-129 do not resolve them, so a verifier cannot determine the expected CRC for a configuration block.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the covered byte range and treatment of the reference bytes, then state the decided coverage.

findings.description: The requirement calls for a CRC over one segment per cycle but does not specify how segments cover the image or how their results form the full-image CRC used by SYS-SUP-023. Rechecking one segment or independently calculating segment CRCs can satisfy the stated segment behavior without checking the full image.
findings.requested_change: Define the segment progression and the relationship between the segment processing and the completed full-image CRC.

findings.description: The requirement explicitly leaves fault-report priority undecided when a service answer is already being transmitted. CON-SUP-139 gives fault reports priority, and CON-SUP-112 requires a report within 10 ms; the required line behavior for this case is therefore incomplete.
findings.requested_change: Decide and specify the line behavior when a fault report arises during transmission of an answer, including its relationship to the report deadline.

findings.description: The statement combines independently testable reporting obligations for STARTUP, OPERATIONAL, SAFE and LATCHED with the separate obligation to count a code 8 report toward the latch rule. One state or the counting behavior could fail while the others pass.
findings.requested_change: Separate the independently testable state-reporting behaviors and reference the code 8 counting obligation in SYS-SUP-035.

findings.description: The phrase 'only after 60 s' prohibits an early count reset but permits the count never to be reset. CON-SUP-117 and CON-SUP-140 require the latch decision to distinguish detections separated by 60 s of fault-free operation, which cannot be assured if an old count persists indefinitely.
findings.requested_change: Specify when the count is cleared once the qualifying fault-free operating time has elapsed, consistent with CON-SUP-135 and CON-SUP-136.
